Management Plan

- Clearly summarize key management actions, treatments, and recommendations provided:
  - Prescribed antibiotics for presumed urinary tract infection (3-day course); patient to start as soon as possible
  - Hydration: recommendation to drink 2.5–3 liters of water daily
  - Cranberry juice recommended; urine-acidifying sachets suggested (to be obtained from chemist)
  - Counseling provided: monitor symptoms; seek re-evaluation if pain worsens, high temperature develops, or if there are ongoing urinary issues or recurrence
  - If symptoms do not resolve or worsen, or if recurrent infections occur, follow-up discussion warranted
  - Pharmacy arrangements: prescription sent to Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy; pickup expected in about an hour; patient to collect at lunchtime
  - No follow-up needed if symptoms resolve; contact again if not resolving or worsening
- Immediate interventions, follow-up appointments, or patient education:
  - Start antibiotic course promptly
  - Increase fluid intake; consider cranberry juice and urine-acidifying sachets
  - Reassess if red flags develop (fever, worsening pain, inability to pass urine)
  - Ensure patient picks up prescribed medication; provide contact if issues arise
